15.solution: Barium sulphate is insoluble (so non-toxic when swallowed) and opaque to X-rays.

35.solution: The coordination number counts the ligand donor atoms bonded to the metal, that is the number of coordinate bonds. It equals the number of ligands only when all are monodentate.

38.solution: In this coupling the diazonium ion is the electrophile; it replaces the H para to OH on the phenol ring, giving p-hydroxyazobenzene. That is electrophilic aromatic substitution.

39.solution: Acidified dichromate oxidises a primary alcohol to the aldehyde and then on to the carboxylic acid.

40.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Acidity
40.solution: Phenols are more acidic than alcohols, and a p-nitro group stabilises the phenoxide further. Among alcohols, the three methyl groups of tert-butanol destabilise its anion, so methanol is the stronger acid.

41.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
41.solution: tert-Butyl alcohol is \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3COH}\): carbinol (\(\mathrm{CH_3OH}\)) with three H replaced by methyl groups, trimethyl carbinol.

42.solution: \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\) reduces a carboxylic acid to the primary alcohol: acetic acid gives ethanol.

43.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
43.solution: The most electronegative halogen, fluorine, withdraws electrons most strongly, so fluoroacetic acid is the strongest acid (least pKa).

44.solution: N-Ethylethanamine, \(\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_2NH}\), has two alkyl groups on N and the formula \(\mathrm{C_4H_{11}N}\). A and B are primary; C is tertiary (and \(\mathrm{C_4H_{11}N}\) too).

45.solution: Sodium and ethanol reduce \(\mathrm{R{-}C{\equiv}N}\) to \(\mathrm{RCH_2NH_2}\), a primary amine (the Mendius reduction).

46.solution: An essential amino acid cannot be made in the body and must come from the diet.

47.solution: Proteins are polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

48.solution: Zinc butyl xanthate is a vulcanisation accelerator: it speeds up the cross-linking of rubber by sulphur.

49.solution: Viscose rayon is regenerated cellulose, which microorganisms break down. Nylon 6 and nylon 6,6 are not biodegradable.

50.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
50.solution: Cinnamon yields cinnamaldehyde, an antimicrobial substance used in remedies for colds. Wintergreen gives methyl salicylate (a pain reliever), and gooseberry and citrus are valued for vitamin C.

52.solution: Need \(-1 \le \log_{1/2}\dfrac{x^2}{2} \le 1\). The base is below 1, so \(\dfrac{1}{2} \le \dfrac{x^2}{2} \le 2\), that is \(1 \le x^2 \le 4\): \([-2, -1] \cup [1, 2]\).

53.solution: \(\tan\theta + \cot\theta = \dfrac{2}{\sin 2\theta}\), so \(\tan 9^\circ + \tan 81^\circ = \dfrac{2}{\sin 18^\circ}\) and \(\tan 27^\circ + \tan 63^\circ = \dfrac{2}{\sin 54^\circ}\). The value is \(\dfrac{2(\sin 54^\circ - \sin 18^\circ)}{\sin 18^\circ\sin 54^\circ}\). Here \(\sin 54^\circ - \sin 18^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\sin 18^\circ\sin 54^\circ = \dfrac{1}{4}\), giving 4.

54.solution: \(\sin^2 2x = 2\cos^2 x\) gives \(2\cos^2 x(2\sin^2 x - 1) = 0\). So \(\cos x = 0\), \(x = (2n + 1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), or \(\sin^2 x = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(x = m\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{4}\). With \(\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\beta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\): sum \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\), product \(\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}\), giving \(8x^2 - 6\pi x + \pi^2 = 0\).

55.subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
55.solution: With \(a = k\sin A\) etc., the condition becomes \(\cot A = \cot B = \cot C\), so the triangle is equilateral. Its area is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 4 = \sqrt{3}\).

63.solution: The tangent is \(x - 2y = 5\). The second circle has centre \((4, -3)\) and radius \(\sqrt{25 - k}\); its distance from the line is \(\dfrac{|4 + 6 - 5|}{\sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{5}\). So \(25 - k = 5\), \(k = 20\) and \(\dfrac{k}{5} = 4\).

64.solution: \(\sqrt{5}x - y = 2\sqrt{5}\mu\) and \(\sqrt{5}x + y = \dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{\mu}\). Multiplying removes \(\mu\): \(5x^2 - y^2 = 20\), that is \(\dfrac{x^2}{4} - \dfrac{y^2}{20} = 1\).

65.solution: \(1 - \cos u \approx \dfrac{u^2}{2}\) with \(u = 1 - \cos x \approx \dfrac{x^2}{2}\), so the numerator is about \(\dfrac{x^4}{8}\) and the limit is \(\dfrac{1}{8}\).

66.subtopic: Logical Equivalence and Algebra of Statements
66.solution: \(\sim(p \to q) \equiv p \wedge \sim q\) and \(\sim(p \wedge r) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim r\). Distributing \(\wedge\,p\): \((p \wedge \sim q) \vee (p \wedge \sim r) \equiv p \wedge (\sim q \vee \sim r)\).

67.solution: The contrapositive is equivalent to the statement itself, \((p \vee q) \to r\), whose negation is \((p \vee q) \wedge \sim r\).

68.solution: The dual is \((p \vee q) \vee \sim(p \wedge q) \equiv p \vee q \vee \sim p \vee \sim q\), which is always true.

69.solution: \(|A| = 1\), so \(A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{-1} + B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\). Then \(x - 2y = 0\) and \(-2x + 3y = -2\) give \(y = 2, x = 4\), so \(x + 3y = 10\).

74.solution: Taking logs, \(y\log x + x\log y = 0\). Differentiating: \(y'\log x + \dfrac{y}{x} + \log y + \dfrac{x}{y}y' = 0\), so \(y' = -\dfrac{y/x + \log y}{\log x + x/y} = -\dfrac{y + x\log y}{x + y\log x} \cdot \dfrac{y}{x}\).

76.solution: By similar triangles \(r = \dfrac{h}{2}\), so \(V = \dfrac{\pi h^3}{12}\) and \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi h^2}{4}\dfrac{dh}{dt}\). At \(h = 6\): \(9\pi\dfrac{dh}{dt} = -2\), so the level falls at \(\dfrac{2}{9\pi}\) ft/sec.

82.solution: \(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{1 + x(x - 1)} = \tan^{-1}x - \tan^{-1}(x - 1) = \tan^{-1}x + \tan^{-1}(1 - x)\). By the property \(\int_0^1 f(1 - x) = \int_0^1 f(x)\), the integral is \(2\int_0^1\tan^{-1}x\,dx\), so \(k = \int_0^1\tan^{-1}x\,dx\).

83.solution: \(\dfrac{1}{(x^2 + 1)(x^2 + 16)} = \dfrac{1}{15}\left(\dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} - \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 16}\right)\), so the integral is \(\dfrac{1}{15}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{40}\). Then \(k^2 - 9 = 40\) and \(k = \pm 7\).

The centre of mass is \(\left(\dfrac{m L/2}{3m}, \dfrac{2m L}{3m}\right) = \left(\dfrac{L}{6}, \dfrac{2L}{3}\right)\).

107.solution: Disc: \(I = \dfrac{MR^2}{4} + MR^2 = \dfrac{5}{4}MR^2\). Ring: \(I = \dfrac{MR^2}{2} + MR^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}MR^2\). The radii of gyration are in the ratio \(\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{4}} : \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \sqrt{5} : \sqrt{6}\).

142.solution: The dark band between the 4th and 5th bright bands has path difference \(\dfrac{9\lambda}{2} = 4.5 \times 6 \times 10^{-5}\) cm \(= 2.7 \times 10^{-4}\) cm.

143.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
143.solution: The central maximum of one slit has width \(\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}\); fitting ten fringes of width \(\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\) needs \(\dfrac{2}{a} = \dfrac{10}{d}\), so \(a = \dfrac{d}{5} = 0.2\) mm.

145.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
145.solution: Moving the source away only lowers the intensity. The stopping potential depends on the frequency, which is unchanged.

146.solution: In a stationary orbit the electron does not radiate, although its velocity keeps changing direction (it is accelerated).

148.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain

149.solution: A NAND gate with its inputs joined is a NOT gate, so the NOR output is inverted twice: \(Y = \overline{A + B}\), a NOR gate.

150.subtopic: p-n Junction — Depletion Layer and Biasing
150.solution: A diode is forward biased when its p side (the arrow's tail) is at the higher potential. Only circuit A has that, with \(+2\) V on the p side and \(-2\) V beyond.
